CEO: major contracts included satellites for Luxembourg and Turkey, air surveillance systems for Qatar and radars for the UAE; Europe order intake was up 46% organically; he expects strong, robust defense order momentum for the full year from Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Southeast Asia.

CFO: the defense revenue outlook has moved from high single-digit to a low double-digit growth potential, and the margin can stay above 13.5%. CEO: the SAMP/T NG outperforms Patriot and is available around 2028 versus around 2032 for Patriot, with prospects including Ukraine, Greece, Nordic countries and the Middle East.

Space profitability turned positive and space growth is expected to be low single digit for the rest of the year; the CEO targets a linear progression to around 7% space operating margin by 2027. Avionics original equipment follows Airbus and Boeing production rates (the CEO says Thales is not the bottleneck for Airbus), while lower air traffic in the Middle East slightly reduced aftermarket activity.
